measures.action: Shut off the ventilation of the burning module (intermodule ventilation valves and cabin fans) so the air stops moving.

effect.text: Engineering proposal (hypothesis for the engine): with no airflow a flame at 21 % O2 in 0 g starves, so the engine stops or slows the spread from the moment the measure is applied. The action is part of the documented ISS fire response (the alarm removes rack power, closes the intermodule ventilation valves and the cabin fans). Its effect on a real module fire is not tested: ACME BRE burned gas flames that emulate solids in still air.
effect.src: Action: NTRS 20030053429 (Overview of ISS U.S. Fire Detection and Suppression System, 2001). Effect: PSI-20 ACME BRE, DOI 10.60555/vb93-3y72 (reported by the authors); hypothesis for modules

gaps: No PSI/NTRS combustion test exists for the inside of any ISS module as a whole. Spread speeds are the SAFFIRE anchor scaled by estimated factors, and a module is treated as one 'plastic' material class.

Module-to-module paths assume an open hatch and continuous fuel (worst case) and hatch-to-hatch distances of 1.5-2 m taken from typical module sizes; no interface drawing was used. The adjacency itself (which module attaches to which) comes from public descriptions read in this session, not from a NASA configuration document; the NASA 'Elements' fact sheet could not be retrieved.

Energetic components: none verified. The Quest high-pressure gas tanks, the truss batteries and the oxygen generation assembly were not verified with a source here, and none is a separately selectable mesh of the 3D model, so the ISS has no rupture in the component engine.

Harmony and Tranquility are one mesh and one material in the model, so they are one component: it is linked to Destiny, Unity, Columbus, Kibo, the Cupola, BEAM, PMM and Bishop, which makes the paths between those modules shorter than the real ones.
All PMAs share one material: only the PMA-1 link (Zarya to Unity) is modelled. Linking it to Harmony would create a false shortcut.

The exterior (truss, solar arrays, carriers, payloads, Kibo's exposed facility, insulation blankets) is outside the pressurised volume: without an oxidiser a flame cannot burn there, so those parts are not simulated.
Mesh IGOAL_SSREF_13 has no material and nothing visible when isolated in the labelling tool; it is declared ignored by mesh name and was not identified.
Portable fire extinguishers (CO2 in the US segment, water foam in the Russian segment; NTRS 20130011664) are not an engine measure: the engine cannot yet model local suppression.

The modules are labelled by the material names of the model (manual labelling by eye, confidence medium); the 'Russian docking and mini-research modules' component groups three materials and the 'Cupola node' component takes the material name Node.Cupola at face value.
